source.institution: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art Archives
source.method: Read born-digital Smithsonian page transcriptions embedded alongside page facsimiles, cross-check selected originals visually using local PyMuPDF rendering; no OCR and no source modification.
source.copyright_note: Only page locators, factual field summaries and brief excerpts persisted. Images/PDF not republished.

april_1909_voucher24.document: Art voucher No. 24 in Freer financial papers (1909 April)

banking_account.name: Maurice Nahman
banking_account.signatures: J. M. Kennedy, C. L. Freer and assistant cashier (bank/Freer representatives), not established as Maurice Nahman's own signature

purchase_schedule.description: S.I. 176-185 Byzantine gold and related collection acquired from Maurice Nahman Cairo, attributed to voucher 24

september_1909_consular_control.signatures_and_seals: Deputy Consul General certification and J. W. Congdon & Co. agent declaration are on the form; no independent autograph by Maurice Nahman identified.
september_1909_consular_control.letterhead: US consular standard form; not Nahman & Co. letterhead
september_1909_consular_control.comparison_significance: Same kind of consular documentation as Bowdoin May 1904, but different dealer string; provides near-contemporary person/company form control only.

september_bank.transfer: GBP 895 to Maurice Nahman care of Credit Foncier Egyptien, Cairo, through Credit Lyonnais, paid September 1909
september_bank.meaning: care-of banking destination, not independent proof of storefront street address

shipping_agents.evidence: J. W. Congdon & Co shipping/account correspondence for three cases of antiquities dispatched under Nahman's instructions by S.S. Istria; shipping-agent identity is distinct from dealer

global_embedded_transcript_search.exact_nahman_and_co_absence_only: Embedded searchable transcriptions do not have that exact string. Not equivalent to having visually audited all 825 original pages.

bowdoin_comparison.reported_historical_record: May 1904 consular certificate mentions Nahman & Co. as dealer, route Cairo to New York
bowdoin_comparison.conclusion: Nahman & Co. (1904) to Maurice/M. Nahman (1909) is plausible documentary lead, NOT a verified same legal business entity.
